method: Static reverse engineering; no specimen or dropped code was executed. Atomscan output and reported reputation were leads. Every original sample received atomscan and cleave facts. The extracted shortcut and batch, embedded XOR PE, and upstream PowerShell were inspected separately.

samples.identification: Saved GitHub source-view page for Chris Campbell / obscuresec Invoke-TwitterBot, ShmooCon IX assessment demonstration
evidence: The submitted bytes are HTML, not an executable PowerShell script. Source is stored as GitHub code-view rawLines and displayed by the page.

All 947 source lines were extracted; they match the public raw GitHub release after normalizing line endings and final newline. The fetched script SHA256 is 8ef32cf815363f34936e1950d15a08e2dee09208e815271444116c8c9c74fa88.
The upstream README describes code released for ShmooCon talks; the script identifies Chris Campbell, a BSD 3-Clause license, and a Twitter-controlled assessment bot.

Loading the PowerShell defines Invoke-TwitterBot. Calling it enters Invoke-Bot, waits, then checks the configured kill date 2013-02-16 before obtaining Twitter instructions. Engagement IP and work-hour guards follow.

The implemented task path retrieves timeline XML, selects statuses.status.text, splits command fields and dispatches shell execution, download/evaluation, file upload, credential prompting, screenshot capture and Startup installation.

Defined routines implement polled key recording, accepted-client cmd.exe stream relay and LSASS token duplication/assignment. Their dispatcher names do not match the definitions (KeylogCommand vs KeyLog, BindShellCommand vs BindShell, GetSystemCommand vs GetSystem), limiting activation as shipped.
The encoded Startup command decodes to $A = GC $env:ProgramData\cache.db; IEX $A. The constant is real code; it is not an opaque second-stage mystery.
samples.judgment_basis: The saved source view, independently matched public conference release, assessment safeguards and expired configuration tip the balance toward a research artifact. No deployment authorization or evidence of unauthorized execution is supplied. Reconfigured operational use would require a different contextual judgment.
samples.trait_policy: Retain accurate offensive capability/objective patterns in the fetched script under the queue instruction separating verdict from severity. Do not install a package/page exception. The direct HTML scan has zero suspicious or hostile findings; following references still inherits the scanner-generated dependency verdict, which YAML cannot rewrite.
changes: Describe the required Twitter matcher as fetched timeline tasking rather than claiming its conditions require polling.
Move the GitHub CDN host reference to communications/url/host/name and the HTML catalog meta property to metadata/document/html, preserving the existing exception consumers.

samples.identification: 32-bit Windows remote-tasking bot/worm with copied Avira version metadata; Avzhan signature lead
evidence: CRT entry at VA 0x4094ee calls the main routine at 0x408640, which starts multiple worker threads, including network/share and drive-propagation workers.

At 0x407b91, the network handler receives a 0x404-byte packet into a buffer; the leading task number is dispatched through conditional branches. Task 8 reaches 0x407f02, passing shutdown -r -t 0 -f to the imported system function.

Main calls the process-kill helper at 0x408572 with named security-product images, including KSafeTray.exe and KSWebShield.exe. The helper walks PROCESSENTRY32 records, compares the supplied name, opens the selected PID with 0x1f0fff access and calls TerminateProcess at 0x40862d.

The share worker resolves WNetAddConnection2A, builds remote IPC/admin-share paths, and tries username/password tables. At 0x406d32 and related sites it copies its current module to remote admin$/C$/D$/E$/F$ paths. At 0x406e9b it formats a remote AT command and at 0x406eaf calls WinExec.

The drive worker enumerates logical drives and classifies them, stages its executable under a recycle-bin-style path, and writes [autorun], OPEN and shell open/explore commands through fopen/fputs beginning at 0x40710b.

At 0x404ab0 the byte loop XORs 0x2200 bytes at VA 0x401180 with 1. The decoded PE was extracted from file offset 0x580 and inspected as a scrnsave-style companion. At 0x404b0d those decoded bytes are written to a supplied output file.
The unsigned artifact claims Avira AntiVir engine identity, which conflicts with its task dispatcher, security-process killing and self-propagation.
samples.judgment_basis: Autonomous self-propagation, named defender termination, remotely triggered forced reboot and deceptive security-vendor identity establish malicious behavior independently of the ML score or supplied sandbox/AV reports. No legitimate deployment context is supplied. The collector filename does not establish Gh0st, Remcos or WannaCry; no ransomware claim is made.
changes: Existing hostile behavior detections are supported and retained.

samples.identification: Invoice/document shortcut with concealed nested ZIP and batch/Python downloader
evidence: The PDF-named .lnk actually targets cmd.exe, requests hidden execution and runs conhost --headless cmd /c powershell -nop.

PowerShell opens the original ZIP from Downloads, gets the member named dot, and writes its content to a temporary ZIP. Tar extracts config.ini; copy writes that content as prep.bat; the final chained command invokes prep.bat.
The dot member is another ZIP. Its config.ini contains a full batch program, not settings. It was safely extracted and reviewed without execution.

The batch relaunches hidden, copies itself into a StateCache directory, opens a downloaded invoice.pdf decoy, and sends username, campaign status and antivirus inventory to remote HTTP endpoints using curl.

A Startup batch file is emitted as a redirected block. Its hidden relauncher refreshes a remote batch file, calls it, waits about 30 minutes with ping, and repeats. The main batch also self-updates and honors a remote REST response.

The script downloads an embedded Python runtime archive and several .pyd/.dat pairs, then launches python.exe with those files and a campaign argument. The fetched stage bytes were not supplied; the suffixes alone do not establish native modules, credential theft, a RAT family or ransomware.
samples.judgment_basis: Document deception, concealed executable script content, hidden execution, recurring remote-code retrieval and Startup activation are concrete hostile behavior. There is no supporting legitimate installer purpose or authorized assessment context.
changes: Replace the arbitrary two-feature script-chain conviction with a file-execution objective requiring archive extraction, configuration-to-batch copy, chained batch invocation and headless execution.
Remove false TEMP-directory-as-EXE-download and icon-prefix-as-working-directory claims. Use canonical notable path/argument facts; consolidate duplicate conhost observations.
Detect the batch Startup redirection block, and require the Startup destination to occur on the copy command itself before reporting copying into Startup.
Relocate antivirus inventory to discovery and PowerShell invocation flags to process arguments; these do not establish Defender bypass or string-concatenation obfuscation.
samples.analysis_limit: The archive walker omits the unsafe dot member and does not analyze its nested script. The original archive is convicted by its parsed shortcut arguments, with two independent local hostile objectives. The manually extracted batch receives its own accurate facts when scanned in isolation.

canonical_moves: TEMP directory-query APIs move from fs/path/temp to os/sysinfo/directories, retaining scope and exact consumers.
The executable copy/sync subcommand text moves from fs/file/copy to process/argument/subcommand.
PDF-plus-LNK suffix is a notable extension observation; execution/deception composites provide the intent claim.
retired_claims: An arbitrary pair of PowerShell mention, NoProfile, TEMP path or similar argument features does not establish a script dropper.
Repeated TEMP references alone establish neither a download nor an EXE.
A SystemRoot/System32 prefix in an icon field does not establish the working directory.
taxonomy_review.migration_notes: No directory was split and no global or per-directory budget was raised. Source scopes and exact consumers were preserved on the ancillary directory-query/subcommand moves. The destination-based copy correction and arbitrary-pair retirement intentionally reduce unsupported coverage. New archive-copy/launch conditions assert co-occurring operations in one parsed argument field; manual reverse engineering verifies the actual same-file chain in this sample.

verification.controls: check.py generates 15 sanitized positive and near-miss controls, including arbitrary filenames, INI/CFG and BAT/CMD variants, absent copy, absent invocation, absent headless execution, NoProfile alone, TEMP references, Startup writes versus references, actual Startup copy versus unrelated copy, and antivirus inventory. All pass.
verification.scans: Original artifacts rescanned; linked raw PowerShell URL confirmed in isolation before/after and source batch rescanned separately. Full reports remain in the session scratch directory.
verification.validation_fixture_review: Full validation exposed a synthetic invoice shortcut whose only content is -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -NoProfile -WindowStyle Hidden cmd /c update.txt. It has no target or staged payload. Its obsolete minimum of two hostile findings depended on the retired generic pair; expectations now require the supported document lure plus existing command observations, with minimum one hostile finding and score floor 190. No second hostile behavior was invented to satisfy the fixture.
